CHIEF COMPLAINT
Cough

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 74-year-old male presenting with cough that started approximately one week ago with yellow sputum production. He reports feeling worse over the last two days. He endorses feeling warm but denies taking his temperature and denies fevers or chills. He reports feeling achy at times. He denies shortness of breath. He has nasal congestion with drainage down his throat and some sinus pressure. No one else in his household is sick. Additionally, this morning while coughing, he fell down approximately 4-5 stairs and twisted his right knee. He reports right knee pain mostly on the inside but is able to walk with a slight limp. The knee does not feel like it will give out. He denies taking pain medication for the knee and has been taking over-the-counter Dayquil for his cough and cold symptoms with minimal relief.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for cough with yellow sputum, feeling warm, achiness, nasal congestion with throat drainage, and sinus pressure. Negative for fevers, chills, and shortness of breath.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension
Diabetes

MEDICATIONS
Lisinopril 20 mg daily
Metformin 1000 mg twice daily
Over-the-counter Dayquil

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works as a teacher. Lives with wife who assists with managing his medications. Cleveland Browns fan.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: Temperature 98.4°F, Blood Pressure 125/62, Heart Rate 80s, Oxygen Saturation 97% on room air
Facial Exam: Pain to palpation of bilateral maxillary sinuses
Nasal Exam: Erythema and edema of nasal turbinates bilaterally with yellow discharge
Throat Exam: Uvula midline, no erythema, edema, or exudate in peritonsillar space
Neck Exam: Bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy
Lung Exam: Coarse rhonchi present bilaterally that clears with cough
Heart Exam: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmur
Right Knee Exam: Pain to palpation, decreased flexion and extension, ecchymosis to right medial knee, no effusion

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Cough/Viral syndrome with mild bronchitis: Likely viral syndrome with mild bronchitis. Recommended continuation of over-the-counter medications. Prescribed guaifenesin 600 mg twice daily. No antibiotics at this time. Patient instructed to call if symptoms worsen; will consider chest x-ray to rule out pneumonia if symptoms worsen.

2. Right knee pain/Right medial collateral ligament strain: Right medial collateral ligament strain from fall this morning. Prescribed meloxicam 15 mg once daily. Referral to physical therapy. Ordered right knee x-ray to rule out bone injury.

3. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily. Ordered lipid panel.

4. Diabetes: Ordered hemoglobin A1c. Patient counseled on importance of monitoring sugar intake and checking blood glucose. Patient instructed to report blood sugars through patient portal. Continue metformin.
